summary: Corrected the 3-SHA divergence: graph is 8 commits stale (not 1) but code-structurally near-current; found an undocumented graphify-out/ re-tracking regression (bloat+info-exposure) and a real, asymmetric CI push-race (stamp-last-commit.yml has no retry, update-search-index.yml does).
result_text:
TRACK 7 — Git/CI history integrity & cross-file version-state divergence
Verified against a fresh clone (git log traversal, `git show --stat`/full diffs on relevant commits).

## 1. [HIGH] The "one commit behind" framing is wrong — actual gap is 8 commits, but the CAUSE and real-world impact differ from what the starting finding implies
File: graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md:13, assets/js/last-commit.json, git log

Chronological order (newest→oldest), confirmed via `git log`:
04f3c36 (HEAD, bot stamp) → b0eae20 (feat: update graphify-out, .gitignore) → dce64fb (stamp) → 8bd39bc (fix css) → 4ba9b0e (stamp) → 24d622a (fix mcp config) → 65e46b4 (stamp) → e665b5f (feat v46: mcp server) → **13d686a (stamp — this is GRAPH_REPORT.md's "Built from" SHA)** → de79f25 (docs v45)...

Correction to the task's premise: local clone HEAD (04f3c36) is NOT behind origin — a fresh `git clone` right now lands exactly on 04f3c36, and it is the *newest* of the three SHAs, not the oldest. `last-commit.json`'s b0eae20 is simply 04f3c36's parent (the commit the stamp-bot was stamping) — that's the bot working exactly as designed, not evidence of a stale/behind local clone. The real divergence is only between the graph's label (13d686a) and current tip (04f3c36): **8 commits**, not 1.

Root cause: graphify-out/ was `.gitignore`d for its entire prior history (confirmed via dev-logs/PortfolioWebsite_TRACKER.md, the v19-era entry: "graphify-out/ — 0 tracked files (fully untracked)", excluded specifically because "neither directory is referenced by any page... yet both were being served live by GitHub Pages — a bloat issue and a minor info-exposure issue"). Because it was gitignored, `graphify update .` could be (and evidently was) run locally many times with zero git-visible signal of staleness — nothing to diff. Commit b0eae20 is the *first ever* commit of graphify-out/ (git show confirms all 225 lines of GRAPH_REPORT.md are `new file mode 100644`), and what got committed was simply whatever sat in the local folder — a snapshot generated once, sometime after e665b5f landed (13d686a is chronologically right after e665b5f), and never regenerated since despite 3 more content commits landing.

Actual severity, checked precisely rather than assumed: of the 3 content commits between 13d686a and current tip, only e665b5f (already inside the graph, since 13d686a postdates it) is graph-structurally relevant. The other two are trivial: `8bd39bc` = 1 line changed in style.css; `24d622a` = 7 lines removed from mcp_config.json (JSON config, not code Graphify would AST-parse for call edges). **So despite the label being 8 commits stale, the actual node/edge data (e.g. bootSite() at 33 edges, community cohesion scores) is very likely still structurally accurate** — Tracks 2/3/8 probably aren't working from meaningfully wrong graph data this time, but the *mechanism* that would catch a future graph-invalidating change is broken (see #2), so this should not be treated as reliably self-correcting going forward.

Fix: re-run `graphify update .` and commit as part of every `sync.ps1` invocation that touches JS/py source (it already does this per sync.ps1:~177-182, so the actual bug is that it silently no-ops if `graphify` isn't on PATH or errors — the `2>$null` on that line swallows all output/errors, so a broken/missing graphify install would look identical to a successful stale-preventing run). Add a non-silenced check.

## 2. [HIGH] graphify-out/ re-tracking is an undocumented regression against the repo's own prior fix
File: .gitignore (graphify-out/ line removed in b0eae20), commit b0eae20

`.gitignore` diff in b0eae20: `-graphify-out/` — the exclusion was deleted, and 489 files / 3.8MB were committed in the same commit. This directly reverses a deliberate, documented earlier decision (tracker: untracked specifically to fix "a bloat issue and a minor info-exposure issue" — internal analysis JSON/dev notes being publicly crawlable via GitHub Pages, which has no `.nojekyll`/`_config.yml` exclusion for graphify-out present in the repo, so everything in it is served live again). The v46 tracker entry at the top of dev-logs/PortfolioWebsite_TRACKER.md (which documents the MCP-server feature shipped in the same window) makes no mention of this .gitignore change or the rationale for re-tracking — looks like an unintentional side effect of a broader graphify-out update rather than a deliberate reversal.

Fix: either (a) re-add `graphify-out/` to .gitignore and keep the freshness workflow purely local/manual, or (b) if committing it is now intentional (e.g. so `graphify query` works for cloud/CI agents), document that decision in the tracker and add a Jekyll/Pages exclusion so it isn't served publicly.

## 3. [BLOCKER] Real, asymmetric CI race condition between the two commit-back bots — one side has zero retry logic
Files: .github/workflows/stamp-last-commit.yml:57, .github/workflows/update-search-index.yml:58-67

Both workflows trigger on the same `push` event and both commit-and-push back to main in parallel jobs. `update-search-index.yml`'s own comments (lines 58-61) explicitly acknowledge the race against `stamp-last-commit.yml` and implement a 5-attempt `git pull --rebase` + retry loop (lines 62-67) to handle losing the race. `stamp-last-commit.yml` has no such handling — line 57 is a bare `git push` with no exit-code check, no retry, no rebase. If `update-search-index.yml`'s bot commit lands on origin first (a coinflip — no ordering guarantee between two independently-triggered `push`-event workflow runs), `stamp-last-commit.yml`'s push fails non-fast-forward, the job step errors, and the run goes red — **last-commit.json silently fails to update for that push** with no automatic recovery. It only catches up incidentally on the *next* human push (since the bot-author guard only blocks the workflow from reacting to its own commits, not to a later human commit). This is a real, currently-live gap, not a hypothetical: nothing in either workflow file enforces job ordering, and GitHub Actions gives no such guarantee for two workflows both triggered by the same push.

Fix: give `stamp-last-commit.yml` the same retry-with-rebase loop `update-search-index.yml` already has (lines 62-67 there are a drop-in pattern), or better — merge both bot commits into a single workflow/job so they can't race each other at all.

## 4. [MEDIUM] sync.ps1's fixed 4-second sleep before re-pulling the bot stamp is a timing guess, not a guarantee
File: sync.ps1:243-247

`Start-Sleep -Seconds 4` then a single `git pull --autostash origin main` with no verification that the pull actually picked up a new commit, and no retry/poll if the CI run (which now includes 2 parallel bot jobs, per #3, each with their own runner cold-start + checkout + push time — commonly 10-30s+ on GitHub-hosted runners) hasn't finished within that window. If CI is still running when the 4s elapses, the local `last-commit.json` stays stale in the developer's working copy after `sync.ps1` reports "Workspace is clean and fully synchronized!" — this is a plausible contributor to exactly the kind of local/remote SHA mismatch the task's confirmed finding was worried about (just not the actual cause of the specific 04f3c36/b0eae20 pair, which — per #1 — was correct bot behavior).

Fix: poll (e.g. `git ls-remote` in a short retry loop checking for a new commit authored by github-actions[bot]) instead of a fixed sleep, or at minimum, print a warning if the post-sleep pull is a no-op.

## 5. [NIT] sync.ps1:158 and :230 blindly `git checkout assets/js/last-commit.json` with no check for pre-existing legitimate local edits
Works as designed for its stated purpose (avoiding merge conflicts on the bot-managed file) and is low-risk since nobody should be hand-editing a bot-owned file, but it discards silently (stderr redirected to `$null`) with no "did you mean to edit this?" signal. Not worth fixing unless someone actually hits it.

## 6. sync.ps1's `-PullOnly --autostash` claim — verified accurate, no bug found
Docstring claim ("Pulls with --autostash so your local work is preserved") matches the actual command at sync.ps1:161 (`git pull --autostash origin main`, executed before the `-PullOnly` early-exit at line 163). `--autostash` does what's claimed: stashes any dirty working tree before the pull/rebase-merge, reapplies after. No divergence between documented and actual behavior here.

## Not part of this track (flagging only)
lighthouse-audit.yml (3rd workflow, not in original scope list but exists in repo) triggers on both push and pull_request with no bot-author guard — harmless since it's read-only/no commit-back, but worth noting for whoever owns CI cost/quota tracking, since it runs Lighthouse CI on every PR too, not just main pushes.
